column1: # The seat grammar's shared case table (app#480, ADR-0042; ADR-0034 D2 before it).
# A seat is the workspace / participant name (the `<seat>` in
# grammar has ONE Go definition, identity.SeatPattern; every implementation
# registered below is a copy that this table holds equal (the `make e2e-serve AS=`
# check in the Makefile is an approximation and is NOT registered: the e2e
# harness re-checks the name in Go):
#   - shell: charts/ctf-user/deploy-user.sh (its SEAT_PATTERN), run row by row
#            scripts/preflight-identity.sh read the SAME rows (their PR is the
#            paired one; until it lands they are not checked against this file).
# A row is never dropped to make an implementation pass: the implementation
# that disagrees is the bug. A change to the grammar changes the rows in the
#   - blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored
#   - split each line on its FIRST tab only. `input` may be empty (the line then
#     starts with a tab) and contains neither a tab nor a newline literally
#   - do NOT read it with `IFS=$'\t' read` (a tab is IFS whitespace there, so an
#   - characters that cannot be written literally are placeholders, decoded by
#     letter); the file itself stays ASCII
#   - the set of placeholders is closed. After decoding, a row whose input still
#     contains `{` or `}` is an error of the READER (an unknown placeholder, or a
#     reader that lacks one), not a verdict: the reader fails. Otherwise a reader
#     that forgot a decoder would test the literal text, reject it, and stay green
#     without ever trying the input the row stands for. No seat row spells a brace.
# The grammar these rows hold is ADR-0042's (app#480): 1 to 53 characters of
# [a-z0-9-], the first and the last a letter or digit.
# --- baseline: what the roster actually holds
# --- length: 53 is the longest a Helm release name (= the seat) can be
# --- a trailing '-': a Helm release name must end in a letter or digit
# --- control and bidi characters ({LF}: a trailing newline is not accepted; $ is not a line anchor here)
